result.answer: The original v1 schedule records the project review for Thursday at 09:30 local time. The current instruction supported by the later amendment is Thursday at 10:00 local time: it expressly says that it replaces v1’s time. The records do not identify a geographic time zone, so “local time” cannot be converted to a specific offset from these materials alone.

approaches.description: Read v1 as the original schedule, then apply v2’s explicit replacement statement to determine the current scheduled time.
approaches.reason: Both the original time and the amendment’s new time are stated, and v2 explicitly says it replaces v1’s time.

approaches.description: Treat both listed times as simultaneously operative.

proof_steps.justification: This is the time text in the v1 record.
proof_steps.statement: Extract v1’s recorded time as Thursday at 09:30 local time.

proof_steps.justification: The amendment supplies a new time and expressly specifies its relation to v1.
proof_steps.statement: Extract v2’s time and its statement that it replaces v1’s time.

proof_steps.justification: A record that expressly replaces an earlier record’s time supersedes that earlier time for the current instruction supported by the records.
proof_steps.statement: Apply v2’s replacement statement: retain 09:30 as historical v1 information and select 10:00 as the current time.

proof_steps.statement: Conclude that a timezone conversion is not determined by the supplied records.
